title: Saints as guardians and mediators, and Mary as Queen of Heaven, rejected by Protestants
source_text: LV. Praeterea illud in controversia est, An Sanctos in Christo defunctos celebrare liceat ut generis humani custodes & patronos, quibus rerum nostrarum regimen a Deo commissum sit: Et illos habere ut tales apud Deum Mediatores atque Intercessores, qui omni tempore omnium hominum preces sive corde, sive ore conceptas audire atque percipere, Deoque offerre & commendare possint, ac suis suffragiis ac meritis adjuvare? Praesertim vero, An Beata Virgo agnoscenda sit atque praedicanda ut Regina caeli, & mundi totius, ac creaturarum omnium Domina: ut illa per quam mundus salvatus est, & quae sola omnes haereses interemit: Et an Mater misericordiae, Mater & fons gratiae, vita & spes nostra salutari debeat: quae omnia probat praxis Ecclesiae Romanae. Improbant vero & damnant Protestantes.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover this is in controversy, Whether it is lawful to celebrate the Saints who died in Christ as guardians and patrons of the human race, to whom the government of our affairs has been committed by God: And to hold them as such Mediators and Intercessors with God, who at every time can hear and perceive the prayers of all men conceived either in heart or in mouth, and offer and commend them to God, and help with their suffrages and merits? But especially, Whether the Blessed Virgin is to be acknowledged and proclaimed as Queen of heaven, and of the whole world, and Lady of all creatures: as she through whom the world has been saved, and who alone has slain all heresies: And whether she ought to be saluted Mother of mercy, Mother and fount of grace, our life and hope: all of which the practice of the Roman Church approves. But the Protestants disapprove and condemn them.
pass_b_english: A further point in dispute is whether it is lawful to celebrate the saints who have died in Christ as guardians and patrons of the human race, entrusted by God with the government of our affairs, and to treat them as mediators and intercessors with God who can at all times hear and take in the prayers of all people, whether spoken in the heart or with the lips, offer and commend them to God, and help with their own suffrages and merits.

Above all, the question is whether the Blessed Virgin should be acknowledged and proclaimed Queen of Heaven and of the whole world and Lady of all creatures, as the one through whom the world was saved and who alone has destroyed all heresies, and whether she should be hailed as Mother of mercy, Mother and fountain of grace, our life and our hope. The practice of the Roman Church approves all of this; the Protestants reject and condemn it.
